facts.text: I've been having twitches that I can't control.
I've been making sounds that I can't control.
It all started suddenly, 3 days ago.
It began in my face: twitches, and winking on the left side.
The winking happened up to 12 times a minute.
The whistling came after the face twitches started.
I don't have any other symptoms.
I've been more jumpy than usual.
I keep going over things in my head and can't stop.
I'm not having any thoughts of killing myself.
I'm not having any thoughts of hurting anyone else.
I don't have any medical problems.
My wife and I separated four months ago.
My daughter moved out of the home.
One week before the tics started I went into my daughter's room, the first time since the separation.
I have a court date coming up for alleged domestic abuse.
A former coworker of mine has Tourette's syndrome.

aliases: functional neurological symptom disorder with abnormal movement
gold.reasoning: 1. Tourette’s syndrome was considered because of the co-occurrence of motor and vocal tics — “Differential diagnosis included Tourette's syndrome, dystonia, Parkinsonism, Wilson disease, enhanced physiologic tremor, Multiple sclerosis.” 2. Dystonia was considered given the abnormal involuntary movements — “Differential diagnosis included Tourette's syndrome, dystonia, Parkinsonism, Wilson disease, enhanced physiologic tremor, Multiple sclerosis.” 3. Parkinsonism was considered as movement disorders can present with tremor or bradykinesia — “Differential diagnosis included Tourette's syndrome, dystonia, Parkinsonism, Wilson disease, enhanced physiologic tremor, Multiple sclerosis.” 4. Wilson disease was considered because it can manifest with movement abnormalities — “Differential diagnosis included Tourette's syndrome, dystonia, Parkinsonism, Wilson disease, enhanced physiologic tremor, Multiple sclerosis.” 5. Enhanced physiologic tremor was considered for its tremulous component — “Differential diagnosis included Tourette's syndrome, dystonia, Parkinsonism, Wilson disease, enhanced physiologic tremor, Multiple sclerosis.” 6. Multiple sclerosis was considered as a demyelinating cause of motor symptoms — “Differential diagnosis included Tourette's syndrome, dystonia, Parkinsonism, Wilson disease, enhanced physiologic tremor, Multiple sclerosis.” 7. Organic causes were excluded by the absence of neurologic abnormalities on examination, obviating further testing — “Due to high suspicion of psychogenic movement disorder with very reassuring neurologic physical examination, no follow‐on labs, radiology, or special testing was required to begin treatment.” 8. Psychogenic movement disorder was identified based on sudden onset, stress triggers, suggestibility, and a normal exam — “Basis for diagnosis takes into account a normal physical exam with multiple typical characteristics of PMD that includes, but is not limited to: sudden abrupt onset of symptoms, Movements triggered or worsened by emotional or physical stressors, cessation of movements may occur by trialing a suggested physical treatment…”

leakage.reason: The observation 'involuntary facial movements' contains the gold word 'movement' as a plain description of what is seen; it does not name the disorder.

source_issues: s006 holds two sentences (vital signs; neurological examination).
notes: Index visit: the outpatient presentation 3 days after the sudden onset of tics and vocalizations (s001-s010).

He first denied stressors and disclosed them, and his jumpiness, poor sleep, ruminations and court date, only on further questioning; the facts hold what he discloses and the reluctance is an acting note.

Clicking, blinking, grimacing and hemifacial spasm were observed during the examination only and stay in the observation finding; the patient's own account names facial twitches, left-sided winking and whistling.
Patient fact labels avoid the gold word 'movement' ('tics or twitches'); the clinical term is an alias.
'Review of systems was otherwise negative' is one 'other symptoms' absent fact.
Harmonisation: the single 'vital signs' record was split into one record per standard parameter with the source's word; no oxygen saturation, which the source does not mention.

acting_notes: At first denies any stressors; discloses the marital separation, the daughter's move and entering her room only when asked further (s003).
Mentions jumpiness, decreased sleep, ruminations and the court date only on further probing (s009).
